facts.raw_span: A man in his 50s presented with a 12-year history of itchy eruptions over the whole body
Multiple nodules appeared on the upper back 1 year previously and gradually increased in number and size
extensive, dry scaly patches on the trunk, arms, and legs
Several 0.5- to 1-cm, dome-shaped, red papules and nodules were found on the upper back
Mildly enlarged lymph nodes were observed on the cervical, axillary, and inguinal regions
Routine blood tests, biochemistry analyses, and peripheral blood flow cytometry tests were within normal limits
No atypical cells were found in the peripheral blood
DNA analysis from paraffin sections showed clonal amplification product for the γ-chain of the T-cell receptor
Atrophy of the epidermis with focal orthokeratosis
Extensive, dense infiltrate of lymphocytes in the entire dermis
Small to medium-sized, atypical lymphocytes with focal areas of epidermotropism
Positive for CD2, CD3, CD4, and CD45RO

Routine blood tests, biochemistry analyses, and peripheral blood flow cytometry tests were within normal limits

concepts.why: The patient's presentation of itchy eruptions, dry scaly patches, and dome-shaped nodules, along with the histopathological findings of atypical lymphocytes and epidermotropism, are consistent with Mycosis Fungoides, a type of cutaneous T-cell lymphoma.
The presence of atypical lymphocytes in the skin and the clonal amplification product for the γ-chain of the T-cell receptor suggest Sézary Syndrome, an aggressive form of cutaneous T-cell lymphoma.

The patient's presentation of itchy eruptions and dry scaly patches, along with the histopathological findings of lymphocytic infiltrate, could be consistent with Cutaneous Pseudolymphoma, a benign condition that mimics lymphoma.

The presence of atypical lymphocytes, enlarged lymph nodes, and the clonal amplification product for the γ-chain of the T-cell receptor suggest Adult T-Cell Leukemia/Lymphoma, a rare and aggressive type of blood cancer.

rationales.F02: Nodules on the upper back are more typical of Mycosis Fungoides
rationales.F04: Dome-shaped papules and nodules are characteristic of Mycosis Fungoides
rationales.F07: Absence of atypical cells in peripheral blood rules out Sézary Syndrome and Adult T-Cell Leukemia/Lymphoma
rationales.F08: Clonal amplification of the T-cell receptor gamma chain is a strong indicator of Mycosis Fungoides and Sézary Syndrome
rationales.F11: Atypical lymphocytes with epidermotropism are characteristic of Mycosis Fungoides
rationales.F12: Positive staining for CD2, CD3, CD4, and CD45RO is typical of Mycosis Fungoides and Sézary Syndrome

frontier_selector.rationale: Mycosis Fungoides best explains the combination of skin findings, including itchy eruptions, dry scaly patches, and dome-shaped nodules, along with the histopathological evidence of atypical lymphocytes with epidermotropism and clonal T-cell receptor amplification, without significant evidence against it.
